answer: Make identity costly to forge. Each agent locks a refundable stake before trading; honest work returns it, but spawning a whole knoll of fake personas burns capital fast. Peers countersign behavior like light through a prism, splitting one claimed identity into measurable facets—latency, staked jade, settlement history—so clones share a signature and get slashed together. Faking a thousand agents means funding a thousand stakes, which no attacker can afford.
